_doc: Every tunable assumption in one place. The map, trip planner, demand model and reports all read this file, so they can never drift apart again.

wait._doc: Expected wait = headway / 2, capped (riders time arrivals on long headways). weight = how many in-vehicle minutes a minute of waiting feels like (1 = calibrated plan; 2 is the usual planning value, a sensitivity that needs ridership.asc recalibrated: -0.195 with weight 2 and max_wait_min 15).

access._doc: How people reach stations. Walk to anything within walk_max_m; drive (park & ride) to commuter rail stations and each line's planned termini within pnr_max_km. Garages hold pnr_spaces cars (DART Parker Road ~2,000, TRE/TEXRail stations 175-1,000); each space serves pnr_people_per_space commuters a day (75% full x 1.1 per car x 1.15 with drop-offs). Riders beyond that are scaled away.

congestion._doc: Peak drive times (moving part) grow per_decade from base_year, capped; BRT running time takes brt_share of the increase. TTI travel-time index: about +3% per decade nationally and in DFW. Mild on purpose: congestion forecasts usually overshoot.

competitive._doc: A commute is transit-competitive if transit <= ratio*drive + slack, under the cap, and longer than min_km.

demand._doc: If data/raw/od_tracts.csv (LODES OD aggregated to tracts, see data/README.md) exists it is used directly. Otherwise a doubly-constrained gravity model is synthesized from tract population and jobs, with beta calibrated against the v1 LODES run.

cost_musd_per_km._doc: Capital cost per route-km by mode and grade, 2025 USD. Calibrated to recent US projects: DART Silver Line ~$45M/km (new track on freight ROW), TEXRail ~$24M/km, Houston/Indy BRT $5-25M/km, US light rail $100-200M/km, US subway $400M+/km.

standards._doc: Stop-spacing bands (km) used by validate. Sources in reports/DESIGN_STANDARDS.md.

cores._doc: Downtown cores: proposed metro inside these radii is costed as tunnel.

budget._doc: Flat capital budget (2025 $M per year) with carryover. Spending is spread over each piece's construction years (staging.construction_years). tolerance = share over budget before validation warns.

staging._doc: Rules for staged build-out (dfwt/staging.py, python -m dfwt stage).

geometry._doc: Alignment design limits (dfwt/align.py, python -m dfwt align). Rmin = minimum curve radius (m); Lp = straight platform length (m); tol = how far the fitted alignment may leave the drawn/routed corridor (m) by grade; Ltmin = minimum tangent between curves; jerk/alat govern spiral length; station_move_auto_m = largest station move applied without review. check_radius_m = tightest curve the validator accepts on each mode (commuter trains run on existing freight track, where curves of ~175 m (10 degrees) are common and simply carry a speed limit). straighten_move_max_m = how far a proposed metro station may move onto the direct path between its neighbors to remove a detour (a 10-minute walk). straighten_move_far_m = the same for sharp jogs (60+ degrees). A stop the line would have to double back for (90+ degrees) is dropped from that line.

growth._doc: Zone population and jobs by year (dfwt/growth.py). Multipliers are relative to the base data (2020 population, 2022 jobs) and interpolated between years; the mid case follows NCTCOG Mobility 2050 (12.4M in 2050) and flattens toward 2100 as national growth stalls (Census 2023 projections). low/high are alternatives for scenarios. TOD adds growth within radius_m of stations opened after existing_year (full within full_radius_m), ramping in along a logistic curve (half at ramp_mid_years, width ramp_width_years). Uplift depends on the station's setting (by people+jobs density within 800 m) times a mode factor; net_new_share of it is new to the region and the rest is drawn from elsewhere (rail mostly moves growth around: Cervero & Seskins; NITC station-area studies).

ridership._doc: Daily riders from the commute model (dfwt/demand.py). Each commute's transit share is a binary logit: asc + b_ivt*(drive - transit door-to-door) - b_ovt_extra*(walk/drive access + egress) + 0.125/$ x parking avoided at paid-parking destinations (FTA/MWCOG ranges: IVT -0.02..-0.03/min, out-of-vehicle 2-3x). asc is calibrated so the 2025 network carries today's rail ridership. Transit commuters x telework; daily trips = commuters x round_trip / work_share_of_transit_trips; boardings = trips x boardings per trip (from the load assignment when computed).

calibration._doc: DART light rail ~65k weekday + TRE + TEXRail + A-train (APTA/NTD 2024-25). Local buses are not modeled.

paid_parking._doc: Destinations where parking costs money ($/day, approximate).
